recentItems.title: China's Integrated Circuit Exports Run Hot
recentItems.description:
China's integrated circuit, or IC, exports are heating up this year, powered by an AI-fueled surge in global demand for memory chips and storage hardware.

That demand is palpable at this storage device factory in the southern Chinese tech hub Shenzhen, where workers are readying a shipment bound for Europe, part of the firm’s roughly five million U.S. dollars in weekly exports to the continent.

To meet soaring demand from the EU market and beyond, the company has substantially ramped up capacity this year, with further expansion already in the pipeline.

Elsewhere in Shenzhen, a memory chip maker says the global AI race is supercharging demand across the board, with memory powering much of China's IC export boom.

Customs data shows that China exported 216 billion U.S. dollars-worth of ICs in the first seven months of 2026, up almost 100 percent year on year.

recentItems.title: Cow Manure Bank in China Turns Farm Waste into Tradeable Asset
recentItems.description:
At the foot of the Liupan Mountain in China's Xiji County, a bank that stores not money, but cow manure, is helping grow farmers crops and household earnings.

Farmers bring in wet cow dung and can exchange it for organic fertilizer, which is produced during a 45-day fermentation and aging process.

The head of the manure bank claims they have a secret ingredient that aids in breaking down the cow dung, and that makes it smell nicer: peach peels.

They collect peels from a nearby peach forest and add them to the mixture claiming they stabilize the dung's carbon-nitrogen ratio and remove its odor.

The "Cow Dung Bank" collects approximately 100,000 cubic meters of cow manure annually, producing about 30,000 tons of commercial organic fertilizer.
